description:
This planning application proposes a roof extension to the existing dwelling at 7 Overmead, Sidcup, DA15 8DS, designed to provide additional internal space. The proposal encompasses several key alterations to the property's roof and external elements.

Key aspects of the proposed work include:

Roof Extension: The primary intervention involves extending the existing roof structure. The small front portion of the roof to the extension will be retained, with its tiles renewed. The existing roof plane will be seamlessly continued to create a new, consistent roof plane, ensuring structural integrity and safety without the need for a flash fire break.

Roof Material Renewal: The entire existing roof is to be renewed as part of this scheme. A new red concrete profile tile roof will be installed, ensuring consistency with both the new extension and the original structure of the house.

Rear Alterations: The existing rear kitchen and boiler flue are proposed to be removed. Any fenestrations created in the roof plane as a result of these removals will be infilled to match the new roof.

Side Elevation Parapet Wall: On the side elevation, a new masonry parapet wall will be constructed vertically from the existing masonry of the flank extension. This wall will be capped with a new coping stone, forming a parapet designed to facilitate rainwater runoff to the front and rear of the rainwater goods. The façade of this new parapet wall will be rendered with a new render to match the existing finish like-for-like, extending up to the top of the parapet wall to ensure a consistent appearance from the street and neighbouring properties.

Rainwater Goods: Existing rainwater goods are to be retained or renewed like-for-like. The existing downpipes will be utilised to allow for rainwater runoff to discharge into the existing drainage system, thereby avoiding the need for new below-ground drainage works.

Flank Verge Renewal: A flank verge of the extended pitch portion of the original roof will be renewed with a new wet verge. This is to ensure suitable detailing and that rainwater goods are maintained up to the line, preventing rainwater from running off the roof.

These proposed works aim to enhance the property by creating additional usable space while ensuring the architectural integrity and aesthetic consistency of the dwelling.
